proposal.name: Execute Python application checks with bound observations

issue_plan.name: Execute Python application checks with bound observations
issue_plan.summary: Two ordered pull requests deliver issue #314's directly testable Python application execution adapter. The first prepares reusable isolated sessions and records actual configured test outcomes; the second executes conformance drivers and binds initial and transition observations to calls and state read-backs from the selected implementation. Together they preserve full staged input and dependency evidence, add real Docker validation, and update SPEC.md and README while keeping public gate execution unavailable. The merger records the new execution and observation policy with decision tooling and completes unavailable Docker/network checks on each final PR head.

issues.title: Prepare Python application execution sessions and record actual test outcomes
issues.body:
Deliver the session and runtime-test part of #314, the execution-adapter step of #313 in #294's Python adoption plan. The base provides project.ResolvePythonApplication, verify.StagePythonApplication, PythonApplicationWorkspace.SelectImage, inert component discovery and caller-supplied component attribution. It does not execute existing Python applications. Add a directly callable adapter in internal/verify for preparing a session and executing configured unittest invocations in it. This PR must be usable and tested independently: conformance declarations can be validated and retained, but driver execution remains explicitly unsupported until the next ordered issue adds bound observations. Do not connect verify.Check, verify.Run, the CLI or Python.Check to this adapter. Keep their existing ErrComponents/ErrPythonApplication rejections, model-only behavior, inert discovery and supplied attribution APIs intact. Legacy Python, marked-file checks and TypeScript must retain their behavior; this adapter requires no source annotations or # +nagini marker and never invokes Nagini. Factory drafting, synthesis and proof adapters are out of scope.

Use StagePythonApplication to preserve the full application's layout and bytes. Component references, invocation working directories and explicit inputs are application-relative; manifest model, conformance and code paths remain verification-project-relative under #310's contract. Validate invocation declarations before execution tools or dependency installation. Support command python with ordered arguments -m unittest followed by selected test names or modules, and validate command python followed by the configured conformance driver script and ordered arguments for the next step. Resolve script arguments according to the declared working directory and require the configured driver identity to match. Reject proof invocations, unsupported commands, interpreter/startup options, shell command strings and any request whose meaning cannot be preserved. Never execute declaration strings through a shell or silently replace a requested command, test selection, arguments or working directory. A valid conformance declaration must not stop preparation for tests, but an attempt to execute it in this first PR must return a clear unsupported result, never conformance evidence.

Keep declared invocation identity separate from actual execution metadata: selected target/check and declaration ID, actual pinned absolute interpreter, trusted launcher and its content identity, ordered arguments, container working directory, explicit environment and effective sampling. Define supported sampling values and defaults, record what is actually used and reject unsupported or conflicting values instead of ignoring them. Gate-owned environment and startup controls cannot be overridden by declarations, including interpreter/import-path settings, hash seed, launcher/output locations, sampling controls and proxy settings. Preserve safe application environment values literally. Account for duplicate invocation IDs on different checks with complete target/check/invocation identities.

Prepare dependencies once per session through the workspace's SelectImage and existing toolchain.PythonDepsImage. Preserve the standard-library path with no root requirements, recursive root requirements and constraints, original and canonical hashes, wheel names/versions/filenames/hashes and recipe/base/platform evidence. Verification-local requirements must not replace root dependencies. Keep the immutable selected image in session state and pass it to every execution; expose reusable session state for later ordinary and larger-bound runs without resolving dependencies again. A missing selected image, dependency failure or invalid dependency evidence fails; there is no fallback or silent re-resolution. SelectImage's no-requirements behavior remains unchanged. Image acquisition is separate from application execution; installation network remains confined to the existing dependency-image builder.

Execute through existing Docker isolation and toolchain.Docker cancellation cleanup, offline with proxy suppression, resource limits and no host environment or credentials. Preserve #227/D-0178 startup behavior: pinned absolute Python, no site/user-site processing or implicit source paths, effective PYTHONHASHSEED=0, trusted standard library and runtime before application imports, application root and driver directory before installed libraries, including nested namespace packages competing with regular dependency packages. Installed scripts, .pth, sitecustomize and usercustomize cannot take over startup. Application source must run from the staged layout, with the declared working directory and argument semantics preserved. Do not repurpose the legacy shell-based conformance path to interpret declarations.

Collect per-test execution and outcomes from the actual unittest runner. Identify which configured lexical test declarations really ran, including selections by module and by individual name. Retain failures, errors, skips and diagnostics as distinct from successful completion; a missing, unexecuted, skipped or failed required test cannot qualify for later gate success even when the process exits zero or another test passes. Handle loader/import errors and unsuccessful process completion without losing already observed outcomes or claiming success for incomplete evidence. A selected declaration or passing process is insufficient. Do not infer production target coverage from a test result and do not fabricate assertion records. Return raw outcomes and execution provenance, not proof, model conformance or project assurance.

Bind every result to hashes of the actual staged snapshot: all copied application files, including unselected siblings, resources, tests, driver, manifest, ratified lock, model and local includes, plus dependencies and trusted runner evidence. Keep production scope unchanged. Check snapshot freshness around execution and between uses of the session; prevent or detect input mutation so changed source cannot retain successful evidence under old hashes. Keep generated output separate from input provenance. Original application files must remain byte-for-byte unchanged on success, failure and cancellation. Portable evidence and fingerprints must be deterministic across repeated runs and relocation, excluding host paths, temporary container/run IDs and other execution-only values while preserving meaningful argument and observation ordering.

Add acceptance and regression tests for validation before tools/install, literal arguments and environment, both unittest invocation forms, working directories, declared-versus-actual metadata, test success/failure/error/skip/nonexecution, empty/malformed/missing or mismatched runner output, snapshot changes including unselected inputs, image selection once and reuse, immutable-image failure without fallback, and preservation of public rejections and legacy execution. Doubles may test orchestration but must not replace real Python execution. Add real Docker tests under the prefix TestPythonApplicationExecution using an unchanged task-lifecycle package that imports a sibling, reads a resource and uses an installed third-party wheel, with recursive root requirements/constraints. Also run the standard-library variant. Exercise real test selections and outcomes, non-root working directories, deterministic repeated and relocated runs, controlled startup, effective hash seed, namespace precedence, offline networking, proxy suppression, cancellation cleanup and unchanged original bytes after success and failure. Arrange the tests so the next issue can extend the same fixture with an application entry point that calls the selected lifecycle component.

Update SPEC.md and README in this PR to describe the directly callable session/test adapter, its invocation and evidence contract, and its current limitations. Public existing-Python gate execution and conformance observation collection remain unavailable at this intermediate stage; remove any now-false blanket statement that no direct adapter exists. Changed SPEC bullets cite recorded foundations D-0013, D-0029, D-0047, D-0054, D-0158, D-0168, D-0171, D-0177, D-0178, D-0180 and D-0122 as appropriate, and link #313's ratified child plan at https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/313#issuecomment-6536681769 (sha256:0380e0c90425c12cb24fed241112820b07758fecb6d812130b71424a857d2366) for the extension. Reuse #310's application-context contract rather than changing it. The plumbing build cannot edit decisions/, pinned statements or ratified locks. Merger work: record the new execution-session policy and its dependencies using decision tooling, and run INVARIANT_PYTHON_APPLICATION_EXECUTION_REAL=1 go test ./internal/verify -run '^TestPythonApplicationExecution' -count=1 -timeout 30m on the final PR head, posting passing output. The real suite must run rather than silently skip when that variable is set. Checks requiring unavailable Docker/network and decision recording belong under Merger work and alone do not require a repair.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Bind Python driver observations to selected implementation calls and state
issues.body:
Complete #314's execution adapter after 'Prepare Python application execution sessions and record actual test outcomes' has merged. That PR supplies staged sessions, immutable dependency reuse, supported-invocation validation, raw runtime-test outcomes and full input provenance. Extend its directly callable adapter to execute configured Python conformance drivers and return sampled observations bound to the actual selected implementation. This is the execution step of #313 in #294's adoption plan; TLC checking, report attribution and public gate admission remain the following #313 work, outside #314. Keep verify.Check, verify.Run, the CLI and the legacy direct Python.Check rejection for existing Python, with and without explicit components. Preserve model-only checking, inert discovery, caller-supplied attribution, legacy Python, marked-file and TypeScript execution. No application annotations or # +nagini marker are required; this adapter never invokes Nagini. Factory drafting, synthesis and proof adapters remain out of scope.

Use the preceding PR's session and execution contract, with StagePythonApplication and SelectImage. Execute command python followed by the configured driver script and ordered arguments, from the declared working directory; component references, inputs and working directories are application-relative, while manifest paths remain verification-project-relative. Keep declarations separate from actual interpreter/launcher/arguments/working-directory/environment/sampling metadata. Preserve early rejection of unsupported or unpreservable commands and proof invocations, without shell interpretation or silent command substitution. Reuse one selected immutable dependency image for repeated executions and expose session state usable by future ordinary/larger-bound callers without dependency resolution. Cover both no-requirements execution and recursive root requirements/constraints, retaining original/canonical hashes and wheel evidence. Maintain offline Docker execution, resource limits, proxy suppression and cancellation cleanup, pinned absolute interpreter, controlled startup with effective hash seed 0, trusted runtime/stdlib precedence and application-root/driver-directory precedence over installed libraries including namespace packages. Declaration overrides must not disable these controls. Installation network belongs only to the existing image builder and failures never fall back to another environment.

Define and document a gate-owned driver observation interface in this PR. A driver must exercise surrounding application behavior through an application entry point that calls the modeled component and read the resulting state from that implementation. The collector must associate each observation with the actual selected staged source and lexical symbol, the executed call, driver and complete invocation identity. Establish initial-state read-back as well as pre/post transition read-backs. Verify correspondence between recorded states and the same implementation instance/state involved in the selected call, with call ordering and lifecycle continuity. A driver-authored trace plus a separate list of imported or called symbols is not sufficient. Gate code must obtain and validate call/read-back evidence rather than treating supplied state dictionaries or target names as proof of a binding. The interface must support repeated runs and multiple instances without evidence leaking between them. Explain the concrete binding, supported callable/state-read-back forms and refusal behavior; refuse forms that cannot be soundly bound instead of guessing. Do not modify application source to add instrumentation or annotations.

Reject an unused target, an import-only target, another symbol from the same file, a replaced callable and a driver that touches or calls the real target while reporting a substitute object's lifecycle. Include mismatched initial state and transitions in this rejection contract. Evidence from another invocation, run or instance cannot satisfy the current execution, even when source and driver names are identical. Missing, empty, malformed, stale, incomplete or inconsistent evidence, import failures and runtime failures must produce failed execution with useful diagnostics, never successful observation evidence. Process exit zero, a declared check, a harness import or a list of called symbols cannot establish observations. Missing or unexecuted configured tests, skips, failures and errors from the session remain distinguishable and cannot become passing required runtime checks when a driver succeeds. Do not invent assertion records or infer target coverage from test success.

Return raw execution outcomes, initial states and transition observations with enough validated binding metadata for the following #313 issue to perform TLC checking and component report attribution. Do not return proof, a model-conformance verdict, exhaustive-state coverage or attempted-step coverage. Initially all successful driver evidence is sampled; neither declarations nor legacy harness imports may upgrade it. Effective sampling and actual runner identity must be recorded independently of declarations. Bind the outputs to the full staged input snapshot and dependency/trusted-runner evidence from the session, including unselected siblings, resources, tests, driver, manifest, lock, model and includes, without broadening production scope. Detect input changes before/during execution and session reuse that would make selected source identity stale. Keep meaningful evidence deterministic and independent of host paths and temporary run identifiers while enforcing per-execution freshness; stale output cannot be accepted merely because its portable content looks valid. Keep original application files byte-for-byte unchanged after successes and all failures.

Extend TestPythonApplicationExecution with real Python-in-Docker tests, not only orchestration doubles. Use the preceding PR's unchanged task-lifecycle application with a sibling import, resource read and installed third-party wheel. Its driver must call the surrounding application entry point, which calls the selected lifecycle component. Assert captured real selected calls, exact initial/pre/post read-backs, instance/run/invocation associations, executed test names and outcomes, deterministic repeated/relocated runs, and unchanged original bytes. Include both dependencies and standard-library sessions, reuse the same image without resolution for multiple invocations, and retain controlled-startup/hash-seed/namespace/offline tests. Add real negative drivers for unused/import-only targets, same-file wrong symbols, replaced callables, a touched real target with a substitute lifecycle, wrong initial state, mismatched transitions, cross-instance/run/invocation reuse, malformed/missing/empty output and import/runtime errors. Include stale snapshot and stale output cases and failed or unexecuted configured tests alongside an otherwise valid driver. Regression tests must retain the public existing-Python rejections and legacy execution behavior. Every accepted binding and rejected substitute must be exercised through actual Python; protocol parsing and orchestration doubles are additional tests, not replacements.

Update SPEC.md and README in this PR to document the complete directly callable adapter and observation interface, with a concrete driver example using unchanged application code, supported invocation forms, state-read-back and binding requirements, raw sampled outputs, failure diagnostics and immutable-session reuse. Make clear that public gate execution remains unavailable until subsequent TLC/report integration; no blanket discovery-only wording should obscure the adapter. Cite recorded foundations D-0013, D-0029, D-0047, D-0054, D-0158, D-0168, D-0170, D-0171, D-0177, D-0178, D-0180 and D-0122 on changed SPEC bullets as appropriate, plus the session-policy decision recorded when the preceding PR merges. Link #313's ratified child plan at https://github.com/gitdek/invariant/issues/313#issuecomment-6536681769 (sha256:0380e0c90425c12cb24fed241112820b07758fecb6d812130b71424a857d2366) for the execution/observation extension, and preserve #310's application-context contract. The plumbing build cannot edit decisions/, pinned statements or ratified locks. Merger work: record the new observation/execution policy and dependencies with decision tooling and run INVARIANT_PYTHON_APPLICATION_EXECUTION_REAL=1 go test ./internal/verify -run '^TestPythonApplicationExecution' -count=1 -timeout 30m on the final PR head, posting passing output. The opt-in real suite must execute, not silently skip. Decision recording and checks needing unavailable Docker/network belong under Merger work and alone do not require a repair. Together with the preceding issue, this completes all of #314; do not defer adapter behavior or required tests to the subsequent public gate integration.

Kind: plumbing

usage.summary: Wrote `issues.json` with two ordered issues covering execution sessions and test outcomes, then implementation-bound driver observations, including documentation and real Docker validation. The plan passed check 1 of 4; `repo/` is unchanged.
